title: Use the PCH dummy-string headers, never hand copies

The upstream static void dummy(Vec*) .rodata emission helper is accepted only with a // dummy: emits <symbols> comment naming the anonymous objects it produces in this unit.
This is the SMS exception to no-inert-emission and to the guard-predefine rule in no-symbol-forgery.
provenance: Accepted 2026-09-16 with implemented lint rules; see audits/sms-worktree-source-quality-2026-09-16/REPORT.md Part 4. Owns PCH guard-predefine findings in SMS: the sms_baseline post-scan hook drops the global header_override_macro finding on a line where sms_pch_string_convention reported a guard predefine.

title: No invented helpers or fabricated scaffolding; leave the function nonmatching
summary: Do not invent helpers. A function you add (static, inline, free or member, in a .cpp or a header) must already exist upstream: declared in the pre-change file or a header it includes, declared by the class it belongs to, or named in config/GMSJ01/symbols.txt or orig/GMSJ01/files/mario.MAP (UNUSED entries count). Anything else is an invented helper and is dropped, even when its boundary gains codegen. Restore the upstream code at its call sites and leave the function nonmatching, with no comment.

Real cases dropped from doldecomp/sms #189: static inline planeDistance (MarioMove.cpp, checkCurrentPlane 99.90%) and canHang (MarioPhysics.cpp), and getWaterHitCount (bossManta.cpp, fixed .rodata dedup). None is in the map; each lost its match on revert, and that loss is expected.
Not invented: a name in symbols.txt or mario.MAP, a definition of a method an upstream header already declares, upstream's own helpers, and the upstream dummy(Vec*) emission helper.

Also rejected: #pragma dont_inline / inline_depth and hand-expanded header inline bodies. A // fabricated, // fake, // fakematch or // TODO comment exempts none of these; upstream AGENTS.md lets humans keep marked fakematch scaffolding, SMS maintainers do not accept it from AI.
Markers do not downgrade global findings either: codegen_pragma, novel_pragma, single_use_wrapper and discarded_expression keep their unmarked severity in SMS.
provenance: Accepted 2026-09-16 with implemented lint rules; see audits/sms-worktree-source-quality-2026-09-16/REPORT.md Part 4. Owns SMS pragma marking policy (pragma bullet moved here from sms-temporary-tactics on 2026-09-16): the sms_baseline post-scan hook drops global codegen_pragma and novel_pragma findings on lines where sms_fabricated_marker reported a pragma, and on the closing #pragma dont_inline off that the SMS rule deliberately accepts. force_active stays an error under the global avoid-pragmas-register-asm record. Rewritten 2026-10-13 for the SMS maintainer ruling (Mrkol, Discord, 2026-10-13) and doldecomp/sms #330/#331: markers no longer downgrade SMS or global findings. Extended 2026-10-13 for the user decision on doldecomp/sms #189 (D1, objectives/sms-pr189-split/decisions.md): invented helpers are dropped at any call count unless the map or an upstream declaration names them (sms_invented_helper).

A function that does not match stays nonmatching without a note; report remaining differences in the attempt summary.
Struct offset comments (/* 0x10 */), _pad member names and comments the code already carried are not agent notes.

title: Accessors and inline swaps need evidence they exist

Swapping inlines to make the frame size fit is a fakematch (doldecomp/sms #330). A frame-size, stack-layout or match-percent gain is not evidence.

summary: Pragmas, register keywords and inline assembly are banned in normal decomp source; source that adds them is rejected.
SMS autonomous output has no pragma exception: dont_inline, inline_depth and force_active are rejected outright (sms-fabricated-marker), and any other codegen pragma is an error.
A TODO or fabricated marker next to a pragma does not downgrade the finding in SMS.
This SMS record replaces the global pragma record for SMS workers.

do_not: Add #pragma global_optimizer off, dont_inline, inline_depth or any other codegen pragma.
Mark a pragma with // TODO or // fabricated to keep it.
Use inline assembly outside SDK-like code while reasonable C alternatives remain.

title: Literals stay inline, data ownership needs evidence, and extern in a .c file is banned
summary: Promoting a string, float, or constant into named storage because generated output exposed an address is not allowed; source that keeps such an invented symbol is rejected.

String literals used as asset names, resource labels, assert/report text, and table labels stay inline; replacing one with a generated or global data symbol is a data regression unless maintainer-approved data-ownership evidence explicitly scopes the change as data work. Packed blobs and pointer offsets into them used as a matching dodge are rejected.
An extern declaration in a .c file is banned outright: declare the symbol in its owning header or define the data in this translation unit.

The only permitted named-data case is recorded section-ownership evidence (.data, .rodata, .sdata, .sdata2, .sbss metadata, symbol size/scope, local labels, or split boundaries); section placement is match evidence, and wrong metadata is fixed rather than compensated for with fake C storage.
A section-target change must name the map symbol or consuming function that owns the data it moves, and a section-only acceptance may not regress any function.

Do not add data-ordering helpers (order_sdata2 or any *_order function) or inert emissions to force .sdata2/.rodata/.data order. Leave a data-order mismatch nonmatching, with no comment, unless upstream code or the symbol map shows the original had that helper.
This SMS record replaces the global literals-and-data-ownership record for SMS workers.

title: Write code a human would write; no odd code that only steers codegen
summary: SMS drops code a human would not write, even when it changes codegen. If the only way to match is odd-looking code, restore the upstream form and leave the function nonmatching, with no comment. That loss is expected.

Odd-looking code: repeated identical tests (point != 0 || point != 0, isActorType(X) || isActorType(X)); double negations ((a + b) - -c, -(-x), !(i != 17 && i != 18)); empty if/else bodies the change adds (if (param_2 != nullptr) { }); dead stores (f32 scale = unused.rand(); overwritten before any read); the same assignment repeated with no write in between; self-assignment (x = x;); casts or (void) reads kept only to steer codegen.

Real cases dropped from doldecomp/sms #189: ConsoleStr.cpp point != 0 || point != 0, MtxUtil.cpp (m[0][0] + m[1][1]) - -m[2][2], bosseel.cpp f32 scale = unused.rand(); then scale = ...;, MapObjInit.cpp if (param_2 != nullptr) { }.

Still normal matching: plain extra locals, aliases, declaration order and hand-expanded real inlines that change non-stack codegen, x = x - 1, !!x, split assignments that read the variable, and repeated calls of the same function.

unused.rand();

do_not: Repeat an identical operand of ||, &&, == or != to change register allocation or branch layout.
Write a - -b, -(-x) or !(a != b && a != c) for a + b, x or a == b || a == c.
Add an empty if/else body or a case that only breaks.
Store a value that the next statement overwrites, repeat an assignment, or assign a variable to itself.

title: Steering is a probe, never the fix
summary: A steering edit changes the source form but not what the program does: a temp or alias that only re-spells an expression (s16 tmp = param_3->mRotation.x;), an accessor or inline hop (getColorChan(i) to getColorBlock()->getColorChan(i)), if/else to ?: or an early return, swapped operands, reordered statements or declarations, a typedef respelling (int to s32), the same value written another way (* 0.5f to / 2.0f), a split compound assignment or a respelled boolean test.

A steering edit that moves codegen is useful evidence: it shows what code the original needs. It is not a fix and a steering match is never done. 56 of the 68 #189 exact matches audited on 2026-10-14 were exact only because of steering and fell to 96-99.9% when it was reverted.

Use it as a probe: run steering_check.py check, read its hypotheses, search for the real construct with real_code_evidence (the header inline, the map symbol, the sibling decomp, the right condition, callee, constant or type), write that, and remove every steering edit. If no real construct is found, leave the function nonmatching, with no comment.

Real fixes change behaviour: a literal or constant, a member, a callee, a call added or removed, a condition, a canonical type, control flow, a definition or an initializer. Keep a real fix in its own statement so it is not entangled with steering.
Codegen directives (added volatile, register, #pragma, asm) are rejected outright.

Accessor and inline swaps are also steering shapes; they keep their own evidence rule (sms_accessor_evidence, sms-accessor-evidence), and frame-only operand swaps keep sms_operand_flip (sms-temporary-tactics).
preferred_repairs: Revert the steering edit to the upstream expression and keep only the real construct the probe pointed to.

title: UNUSED functions get a body only when they were inlined
summary: SMS maintainer rule (Mrkol, doldecomp/sms #342 review, 2026-10-15): "UNUSED functions may only be reconstructed when they were inlined into other functions in the same TU."

An UNUSED function is one orig/GMSJ01/files/mario.MAP lists as `UNUSED size ........ mangled lib file` for the unit: the linker dead-stripped it, so the target object has no code of its own for it. Upstream leaves such functions as empty stubs ({ }, return;, return <constant>;) or does not define them.

The mechanical test (stub test): build the unit with the body and with the body replaced by a stub. If a same-TU caller gets worse when the body is emptied, the original inlined it and the body is allowed. If no function present in the target changes, the body is dead and must go.

The evidence must travel with the change: name the same-TU caller that gets worse and by how much (e.g. `TNerveChuuHanaRoll::execute 86% -> 45% when emptied`). A reconstructed UNUSED body without that evidence shown is removed in review even when the evidence exists.

Run the stub test before keeping such a body: `python3 toolpacks/gamecube-decomp/_impl/gamecube/tools/steering_check.py unused-test --repo . --file <file> --function <Qualified::name>`. The steering gate runs it on every touched unit and is authoritative: a dead UNUSED body is a rule violation and the stub is restored.

Review outcome on #342 (commit 360931f3, src/Enemy/chuuhana.cpp lines 554 and 719): Mrkol called the TChuuHana::margeVelocity and TChuuHana::rolling bodies "Made up bullshit, remove. UNUSED functions may only be reconstructed when they were inlined into other functions in the same TU, this one seems to be truly dead code", and both were removed before merge (3ebd9d9c keeps `{ }`). rolling had stub-test evidence (TNerveChuuHanaRoll::execute 86% -> 45% when emptied) but the PR did not show it. TMareEventDepressWall::emitEffect(int) is dead per the stub test; we dropped it from #344 before review (4992225c).
preferred_repairs: Restore the upstream stub, signature kept: `void TMareEventDepressWall::emitEffect(int) { }`.
python3 toolpacks/gamecube-decomp/_impl/gamecube/tools/steering_check.py unused-test --repo . --file <file> --function <Qualified::name>
Keep the body only when unused-test reports `inlined`, and put the evidence with the change: `Evidence-Inlined: TChuuHana::rolling -> TNerveChuuHanaRoll::execute (86.0% -> 45.0% when emptied)`.

title: Decompile in order: construct and declare only classes whose own units are ready
summary: SMS maintainer ruling (Mrkol, closing doldecomp/sms #347 and #348 unmerged, 2026-10-15): "Please leave MarNameRefGen alone, people will fill it in eventually when the relevant stuff is properly decompiled. This is doing things out of order" and "Same here, don't jump the fence please. It will get filled out eventually".

Readiness is per class and bound to a revision (toolpacks/gamecube-decomp/_impl/gamecube/tools/readiness.py). A class's owner unit is the object that strongly defines its vtable, else the object with a strict majority of its strong member functions; ties are ambiguous. `started` means the owner unit's source at that revision actively defines at least one strong member of the class. `construct_ready` means the owner source defines every strong constructor the target object has; a class whose constructors are all weak (inline in the original) is shared and needs no owner code. Header text never grants readiness: an inline constructor added to a header does not count when the target has a strong one. Unit match percentages are context only; no threshold decides readiness.

What is checked: registry files (src/System/MarNameRefGen*.cpp) may construct or reference only classes that are construct_ready or shared. A class, its members, inline bodies or out-of-class member definitions may be added only when the class is started (or shared), in any file including the target .cpp; forward declarations are fine, and a map-absent helper defined only in the .cpp being changed is a TU-local helper. An ambiguous owner, an owner without a source file or a class absent from the map is unresolved and is never treated as ready.

Enforcement: the scheduler defers functions whose target code constructs not-ready classes and blocks registry functions until the classes are ready (the frontier); the edit-scope fence rejects not-ready or unresolved class edits in worker changes; integration re-checks the patch at HEAD (rejected_out_of_scope); publication runs pr_scope_check before pushing (scope_refused); the steering gate's ordering check covers MarNameRefGen. The lints sms_out_of_order_fill and sms_undecompiled_class_decl are the review backstop, with readiness read at the merge base.

Human practice (doldecomp/sms history, order-scope plan section 0, statistics from validation/human_order): registry PR #92 constructed only classes with full declarations (202/202) and later additions pointed at units with source (165/167); 70% of human PRs touch one unit (172/247); PRs that edit foreign headers touch a median of 2 per PR with a median of 6 lines per edit; nobody declared classes whose unit had no source.

Real cases: #347 added `return new TKoopa("クッパ");` and a TKillerManager declaration in include/Enemy/Killer.hpp, and #348 constructed FruitsBoat, Kukku, Killer, BeeHive and Bird classes; all owner units were blank stubs. TTinKoopa (Enemy/tinkoopa defines its constructor) is ready to construct.
